scope: United States physical mail. Read official instructions again before a submission; this file never authorizes contact or payment.

playbooks.title: Mail addressed only to a confirmed former resident
steps: Confirm with the household that the named person no longer lives there. An unfamiliar name alone is insufficient.
For the correct address but an absent named recipient, mark the unopened envelope Not at this address without covering the address and return it to the carrier or a USPS collection box.
For mail delivered to the wrong address, return it to the carrier or mailbox without writing an endorsement or covering the address.
Unendorsed undeliverable USPS Marketing Mail is disposed of rather than automatically returned; contact the advertiser separately if an appropriate verified address-correction route is available.
playbooks.limits: No change of address, account changes, or identity-certified opt-outs on behalf of former residents. Returning an envelope does not prove list suppression.

playbooks.title: Current Resident, Occupant, and address-based advertising
steps: Treat Jane Doe or Current Resident as addressed to the occupant, even when Jane Doe moved away.
For advertising, prepare an address-based promotional opt-out to the verified sender. Do not claim the named person is authorizing it.
playbooks.limits: USPS recognizes occupant and exceptional address formats. A correctly addressed piece is not former-resident misdelivery solely because one printed name moved. No universal opt-out is promised for every saturation mailing.

playbooks.title: Repeated delivery errors
steps: Verify which local delivery office serves the address. Prepare a factual complaint with selected dates and envelope evidence.
A postal customer may inquire or complain at a Post Office by phone, email, letter, or in person. The agent may draft; the person approves any specific contact.
If choosing a letter, verify its destination and preview the exact contents before sending or buying postage.
playbooks.limits: Certified mail is optional, not a required suppression procedure. No PS Form 3982 prescription, correction deadline, or promised outcome is included. A delivery receipt does not prove the requested correction happened.

playbooks.title: Sender-specific catalog requests
steps: Use the sender's official website to verify its postal marketing contact or preference form; envelope links and QR codes are not proof of legitimacy.
Alternatively, Catalog Choice provides a sender search and opt-out workflow. The person should review that service's current account, eligibility and privacy requirements before using it.
Submit only the approved request and record what the sender or service actually acknowledged.
playbooks.limits: The kit has no catalog-provider integration. It does not assert a fixed waiting period or that every sender participates.

playbooks.title: Broader marketing preferences
steps: Visit DMAchoice for the person's own catalog and marketing-mail preferences.
Read the current eligibility, scope and fee on the official site. Obtain approval of the actual fee before paying.
playbooks.limits: This is not a universal stop for all mail or a blanket authority to enroll former residents. Fees are deliberately not hardcoded. The FTC page and provider checkout may have different update dates.

playbooks.title: Prescreened credit and insurance offers
steps: The named consumer can use OptOutPrescreen, the consumer reporting industry's official service.
The official service offers a five-year electronic opt-out; permanent opt-out requires the signed election form returned by mail.
Have the person enter sensitive identity information directly on the official site. Do not put SSNs, dates of birth or signatures in this kit's ledger.
playbooks.limits: A current-occupant request does not authorize changing another person's credit-file preferences. This affects participating reporting companies' firm-offer lists, not all advertising.
